name: TX-30
label: Safe D

key_factors: Post-redistricting district with a 25-point Democratic partisan lean
Haynes has raised over $420,000 plus $200,000 in outside support; Jackson under $18,000
Polymarket prices the Democrat at 96 percent
model.rationale: The district's strong Democratic lean after redistricting, Haynes's decisive fundraising advantage, and prediction markets pricing the race near 96 percent Democratic all point the same way. With no polls to contradict the fundamentals, this stays safely Democratic.
model.watch: Any late-breaking polling showing a much narrower race, or a surge of outside spending for Jackson, would be the first sign of movement.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; fundamentals point clearly one way (post-redistricting), so it is treated as safe for that party.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
TX-30 is an open seat after redistricting reshaped the Dallas-area district, and its new boundaries carry a roughly 25-point Democratic lean. Frederick Haynes III enters the general election with a large financial edge, having raised about $420,000 and drawn $200,000 in outside support, while Republican Everett Jackson has raised under $18,000 with little cash on hand.

Prediction markets put the Democratic nominee's chances near 96 percent, and no expert raters flag the race as competitive. With no general-election polling available, the forecast rests on the district's fundamentals, which point clearly toward a safe Democratic hold.
